## How to use this file

This file replaces the project's `.sliceui/` JSON artifacts, which are largely empty for this
stack (they were generated by an Angular-first scanner). Everything below was read directly from
the repo. The design to reproduce is the image in the chat — reproduce it **exactly**; this file

There is no `sliceui verify` gate for you and no repo access. See the last section.

## Project & framework

- **Next.js 16.3.4** (App Router), **React 19.2.8**, **TypeScript 5 strict**, **Tailwind CSS 3.4**.
  Verified in `package.json` and in `node_modules`. `next.config.mjs` sets `reactStrictMode: true`
  and `turbopack.root`.
- **Write target:** `app/` (this is `componentDir`). A new full route goes in `app/<route>/page.tsx`;
  a new piece of UI goes in `components/`.
- **Routing is file-system based.** `app/<segment>/page.tsx` is a route and is the default export.
  A route folder may need a `page.tsx` to be publicly reachable. Do not create `pages/` (Pages
  Router) — this project uses `app/` only.
- **Server Components by default.** Add `"use client"` **only** at the top of a file that needs
  state, effects, event handlers, or browser APIs. Directives must precede all imports.
- **Next 16 breaking changes that matter for codegen** (read from
  `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/upgrading/version-16.md`):
  - `params` and `searchParams` are **Promises** and sync access is fully removed. Always
    `const { id } = await params` in an `async` page.
  - `cookies()`, `headers()`, `draftMode()` are async-only.
  - `next lint` was **removed**, and `next build` no longer lints. Do not add `eslint` config keys.
  - Turbopack is the default bundler.
- **Styling syntax:** Tailwind **v3** — `@tailwind base/components/utilities` in `app/globals.css`
  plus a JS `tailwind.config.ts`. Do **not** write Tailwind v4 `@theme` / `@import "tailwindcss"`.
- **Path alias:** `@/*` → repo root (`tsconfig.json`). Import `@/components/ui/button`,
  `@/lib/utils`, `@/data/person`.
- **`dark` is a class, not the OS setting.** `darkMode: ["class"]` in `tailwind.config.ts`. The
  site is dark-only by design (a documented, intentional deviation). Do not add a light theme or a
  theme toggle unless asked.

## How this project writes components

**Anatomy of a UI primitive** (see `components/ui/button.tsx`, `badge.tsx`, `card.tsx`,
`input.tsx`, `avatar.tsx`, `separator.tsx`, `tabs.tsx`):

1. `"use client";` only when the file uses hooks or a Radix primitive requiring it
   (`tabs.tsx`, `avatar.tsx`, `separator.tsx`, `reveal.tsx` have it; `button.tsx`, `badge.tsx`,
   `card.tsx`, `input.tsx` do not).
2. `import * as React from "react";`, then the primitive/library import, then `import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";`.
3. Create the component with `React.forwardRef<RefElement, Props>` and set `Component.displayName`.
4. Merge classes with `cn(base, className)` — always `className` last so callers can override.
5. Export at the bottom as a **named** export: `export { Button, buttonVariants };`.

**Variants** use `class-variance-authority`, never conditional class strings in JSX:

```tsx
const badgeVariants = cva("inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-full border px-3 py-1 …", {
  variants: {
    variant: {
      default: "gradient-border gradient-fill border-transparent text-foreground",
      accent:  "gradient-border border-transparent bg-accent/10 text-accent",
      outline: "border-border bg-white/[0.02] text-foreground/80 hover:border-white/20",
      muted:   "border-transparent bg-secondary text-muted-foreground",
    },
  },
  defaultVariants: { variant: "default" },
});
```

Props extend the primitive's own props **plus** `VariantProps<typeof xVariants>`, e.g.
`export interface BadgeProps extends React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, VariantProps<typeof badgeVariants> {}`.

**Polymorphism:** `Button` takes `asChild?: boolean` and swaps `Slot` for `"button"`
(`@radix-ui/react-slot`). Use `<Button asChild>` to render an `<a>`, never a nested `<a><button>`.

**Sections** (`components/sections/*.tsx`) are the opposite shape: no `"use client"`, no
`forwardRef`, plain **named** function exports (`export function Projects()`), importing their
copy from `data/*.ts` and mapping over it. Server Components throughout.

**Pages** (`app/**/page.tsx`) default-export the component, optionally after
`export const metadata: Metadata = { title, description }`. Static demo data is declared as a
module-level `const` array **above** the component, with leaf sub-components in the same file.
See `app/new-page/page.tsx` — it defines `Sidebar`, `Header`, `StatCards`, `RevenueChart`,
`RecentSales` as local functions and composes them in the default export.

**Naming:** files are PascalCase when one component owns the file (`Button`, `SectionHeading`,
`Reveal`) and kebab-case inside feature dirs (`components/ui/animated-shader-background.tsx`,
`components/layout/sidebar-nav.tsx`, `components/sections/about.tsx`). Never two conventions in
the same folder — match the folder you're writing into.

**Mock data** lives in `data/*.ts` as a typed `export const` with an exported `interface` above it
(`data/projects.ts`), and is marked by a `// SAMPLE` comment. Inline page data uses `// TODO: wire to service`.

- **table:** not served by a library. Build a semantic `<table>` with `<thead><th scope="col">`
  and `<tbody><tr><td>` — no library exists here, flag it to the user.
- **select / date / slider / switch / checkbox / pagination / toast / modal / editor:** **none —
  none of these libraries are installed.** Use the native HTML element
  (`<select>`, `<input type="date">`, `<input type="checkbox">`, `<dialog>` …) styled with the
  utilities below, and **flag in your reply that the project has no library for it**. Do not
  import or invent `@radix-ui/react-dialog`, `sonner`, `react-hook-form`, `date-fns`, or shadcn
  components that are not in `components/ui/`.
- **chart:** no charting library. `app/new-page/page.tsx` hand-builds bars with a `%` height div
  and a y-axis label column. If the design shows a chart, follow that pattern rather than adding
  a dependency.

## Styling system

Tailwind utility composition. Class strings are long and explicit, written inline in JSX and
merged with `cn`. Only **four** custom classes exist project-wide — everything else is stock
Tailwind utilities. The two "invisible effect" classes below are the ones you must not miss.

**Custom classes, all defined in `app/globals.css` `@layer components`:**

- `gradient-border` — a 1px conic-gradient ring drawn with `::before` using mask-composite, and
  it **follows the element's own border-radius** (`border-radius: inherit`). On hover the ring
  becomes a bright glint that circles the element (`gb-spin` 1.4s linear infinite).
- `gradient-fill` — the dark metallic body: a radial white highlight at `12% 0%` over a
  `linear-gradient(180deg, hsl(220 12% 16%), hsl(228 64% 4%))`.
- `gradient-shine` — a skewed white bar `::after` that sweeps left→right on hover
  (`left: -70%` → `left: 140%`, 0.7s cubic-bezier). Requires `relative overflow-hidden`.
- `container-page` (`@layer utilities`) — `mx-auto w-full max-w-6xl px-6 sm:px-8`. **Duplicate of
  the shell's own class string; prefer inlining the utilities so it matches `site-shell.tsx`.**

Usage: `<Button>` = `gradient-border gradient-fill gradient-shine`; `Badge variant="default"` =
`gradient-border gradient-fill`. All three no-op under `prefers-reduced-motion` (handled in CSS).

**Recurring card / panel pattern — copy this exactly:**

```tsx
className="rounded-xl border border-white/[0.07] bg-white/[0.02] p-6
           transition-colors duration-300 hover:border-white/[0.16]"
```

With lift (clickable cards only), add
`hover:-translate-y-0.5 hover:bg-white/[0.045] transition-all duration-300`
(`components/sections/projects.tsx`). Sections wrap in
`<section id="…" className="scroll-mt-24 border-t border-white/[0.05] py-16 sm:py-24">`.

**Hover / open / active state inventory (invisible in a screenshot — reproduce these):**

| Element | Effect |
|---|---|
| Button (all) | `active:scale-[0.98]`, `transition-all duration-200`; default variant lifts its glow shadow |
| Button default | `shadow-[0_0_28px_-10px_hsl(0_0%_100%_/_0.4)]` → `…34px…0.5]` on hover |
| Button outline | `bg-white/[0.02]` → `hover:bg-white/[0.06]` |
| Input | `border-border/60` → `hover:border-white/15`, focus `focus-visible:border-white/25` |
| Nav item / sidebar row | `text-white/50` → `hover:text-foreground`; active row `bg-muted text-foreground` |
| Chip / badge outline | `hover:border-white/20` |
| Table row | `hover:bg-muted/60` |
| Bar chart bar | `bg-primary/90 hover:opacity-80` |
| Nav underline | `w-4 bg-white/25` → hover `w-6 bg-white/50`; **active** `w-8 bg-accent` |
| Tabs trigger | `data-[state=active]:bg-background data-[state=active]:text-foreground data-[state=active]:shadow` |
| Toggle icon | `dark:block` / `dark:hidden` pair inside the button |

**Focus — non-negotiable, on every interactive element:**
`focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2
focus-visible:ring-offset-background`. Icons passed alongside `aria-label` must get `aria-hidden="true"`.

**Type scale in use:** `text-3xl font-bold tracking-tight` for page titles, `text-xl font-semibold
tracking-tight` for card titles, `text-sm leading-relaxed text-muted-foreground` for body copy.
Mono micro-labels: `font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-[0.25em] text-white/40` (nav),
`tracking-[0.35em]` (section eyebrow), `tracking-widest` / `tracking-wider` (buttons, badges).
Radius: cards/panels `rounded-xl`, buttons `rounded-full`, inputs/rows `rounded-lg`.

## Page anatomy & naming

- **Route shell.** Marketing pages render inside `SiteShell`
  (`components/layout/site-shell.tsx`): skip-link → `MobileHeader` → fixed decorative shader strip
  → `max-w-6xl` two-column flex where the left `<aside>` is `hidden lg:block w-[320px] xl:w-[380px]`
  with a `sticky top-0 h-screen overflow-y-auto`, and `<main id="content" className="min-w-0 flex-1 …">`
  scrolls. **Then** the sections. Interactive/app routes (e.g. `app/new-page/page.tsx`) deliberately
  **skip** `SiteShell` and own their full-viewport layout.
- **Section skeleton, in order** (`components/sections/projects.tsx` is the best example):
  `<section id> → <SectionHeading index eyebrow title description?> → list/grid → per-item Reveal`.
  Section indexes are zero-padded strings `"01"`…`"06"`, matched to `navSections` in `data/person.ts`.
- **Heading component:** `SectionHeading` (`components/section-heading.tsx`) takes
  `index`, `eyebrow`, `title`, optional `description`, optional `className`; it renders an
  `<h2>` with the eyebrow row `${index} — line — ${eyebrow}`. Reuse it; do not hand-roll an `<h2>`.
- **Lists:** `experience` and `projects` use `<ol>`/`<ul>` + `<li>`, with `<article>` inside the
  `<li>` for a job entry. Match that.
- **`Reveal`** (`components/reveal.tsx`) is the only scroll animation: `<Reveal delay={i * 80}>`.
  It is a client component using IntersectionObserver and it self-disables under
  `prefers-reduced-motion`. Do **not** add framer-motion to new content — it is reserved for
  `components/ui/spotlight.tsx` and the robot card.
- **Handlers:** event props are inline arrow functions on the element
  (`onClick={() => setX(v)}`); there are no separate `handleX` functions for simple UI state.
- No component prefix, no custom event naming, no `::ng-deep` — this is React/Tailwind.

## Design tokens

Semantic CSS custom properties (HSL triplets, no `hsl()` wrapper) declared in `:root` inside
`app/globals.css`, surfaced to Tailwind in `tailwind.config.ts`. **`design-tokens.md` is empty
(`_(none detected)_`) — the verified source is `app/globals.css` and `tailwind.config.ts`.**
Always use the token name (`bg-background`, `text-muted-foreground`), never a hex.

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `--background` | `228 64% 2%` | page field (near-black OLED) |
| `--foreground` | `210 20% 98%` | primary text |
| `--card` / `--popover` | `228 50% 3%` | raised surfaces |
| `--primary` | `210 20% 98%` | near-white; bar-chart fills |
| `--secondary` / `--muted` | `230 15% 10%` | chips, hover rows, avatar fallback |
| `--muted-foreground` | `215 16% 60%` | body copy |
| `--accent` | `199 89% 48%` | **the cyan** — eyebrows, active nav, accent badge, focus glow |
| `--destructive` | `0 63% 55%` | errors |
| `--border` / `--input` | `228 18% 12%` | hairlines (used as `border-border/60`) |
| `--ring` | `199 89% 48%` | focus ring = accent |

`--radius: 0.75rem` → `rounded-lg`; `md`/`sm` are derived. Fonts: `--font-sans` = `--font-grotesk`
(Space Grotesk), `--font-mono` = `--font-jetbrains` (JetBrains Mono), loaded via `next/font/google`
in `components/fonts.ts` and applied as `.variable` classes on `<html>` in `app/layout.tsx`.
Full list: `app/globals.css` (`:root` block) and `tailwind.config.ts` (`theme.extend.colors`).

Common opacity idioms: `border-white/[0.05]` (section rules), `border-white/[0.07]` +
`bg-white/[0.02]` (cards), `text-white/40` / `text-white/30` (metadata), `bg-accent/10`,
`bg-accent/50`, `bg-muted/60`.

## Aturan untuk Agent Tanpa CLI

Five invariants, in this project's terms. Follow all five.

1. **Reproduce only what the design shows.** Build exactly the structure, elements, and copy
   visible in the image — no invented wrappers, extra cards, "helpful" sections, or an `<h1>` the
   design doesn't have. In React this means: one component per visual block, no gratuitous
   fragment nesting, and no component you weren't asked for.
2. **Style the way this project styles.** Compose Tailwind utilities inline and merge them with
   `cn()`; reuse `components/ui/*` for button/card/badge/input/tabs/avatar/separator instead of
   writing new markup. Do not invent CSS classes, do not add a `.module.css` or `styled-components`,
   and do not reach for `gradient-border` / `gradient-fill` / `gradient-shine` unless the design
   actually shows that metallic treatment. Use semantic tokens (`bg-card`, `text-muted-foreground`),
   never raw hex or `hsl()` literals.
3. **Copy the invisible effects.** Hover, focus, active, open, and status states are not visible in
   the image — take them verbatim from the "Hover / open / active state inventory" and the focus
   ring rule above. A slice without `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring
   focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-background` on its interactive elements is
   wrong even if it looks identical to the screenshot.
4. **All data is mock.** Declare demo rows as a module-level typed `const` array above the
   component and mark it `// TODO: wire to service` (or `// SAMPLE` for `data/*.ts`, matching
   `data/projects.ts`). Never invent an endpoint, fetch, service module, or API response shape —
   this repo has no data layer.
5. **Text is literal from the design.** Type the visible strings exactly as shown. No i18n keys, no
   `t()` wrappers, no translation dictionary — this is a slice, not production localization.

Additionally: because this is Next.js 16, keep the file a **Server Component** unless it needs
state, effects, or event handlers — only then add `"use client"` at the very top. If the design
maps to a whole route, write `app/<route>/page.tsx` with a default export and a `metadata` export.
